2_Introduction: Systematic parameter adjustments underlie the fabrication of a perovskite cell that was fabricated, capturing how controlled conditions influence a PCE of 23.8705%, FF of 83.5955%, Voc of 1.1436 V, and Jsc of 24.969 mA/cm². For the perovskite film, 1.73 mol/L precursor solution was prepared according to the chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating onto the substrate using a two-step spin-coating process, first at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. A timed antisolvent drop (160 µL at last 10 s) enhanced the perovskite crystallization kinetics. Heat-treatment was implemented with the substrates for 25 min at 110 °C.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), thereby stabilizing the photoactive α-phase while suppressing δ-phase nucleation and mitigating halide segregation and ion migration—effects further reinforced by the low-dimensional tolerance imparted by Cs⁺ and the entropy-driven stabilization from MA⁺/FA⁺ mixing; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent expulsion), establishes precise control over supersaturation and nucleation density, while the precisely timed antisolvent quench (160 µL delivered at the final 10 s of high-speed spinning) triggers instantaneous phase separation and accelerates crystallization kinetics to favor large, oriented grains with reduced grain-boundary area and suppressed trap-state formation at interfacial and intra-grain sites; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min completes ligand rearrangement, volatilizes residual solvents and intermediates, and promotes Pb–I framework relaxation—thereby lowering non-radiative recombination centers, enhancing carrier diffusion length, and improving charge extraction across both electron- and hole-transport interfaces; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or molecular passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation composition synergizes with the kinetic crystallization control to yield a film morphology exhibiting high spatial uniformity and continuity—as evidenced by optical microscopy and PL mapping showing homogeneous grayscale intensity distribution and absence of pinholes or dark-spot aggregates—while time-resolved PL reveals a monoexponential decay with a prolonged lifetime (τ ≈ 1.24 µs), confirming effective suppression of shallow and deep-level traps, and XRD analysis corroborates phase purity through the complete absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°) and sharp, narrow (001) and (011) reflections with minimal FWHM, indicating low microstrain, high crystallinity, and coherent domain growth—all of which collectively minimize interfacial recombination losses, maximize built-in potential, and enable balanced charge transport, yielding Voc of 1.1436 V, Jsc of 24.969 mA/cm², FF of 83.5955%, and PCE of 23.8705%.
